title: LLM Agents for Knowledge Discovery in Atomic Layer Processing
experiments_summary: Two experimental systems were used to probe LLM agent knowledge discovery capabilities. The first was an 'Alien Market' parlor game where agents used a single tool to query whether words could be purchased, with the hidden rule being rejection of any word containing the letters 'p' or 'm'. Multiple LLM models (gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.0-flash) were tested using a LangChain ReACT framework. In the first experiment set, agents ran without constraints on number of queries (5 iterations each). In the second set, agents were explicitly instructed to perform n experiments (n = 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90), with three iterations per condition. Conclusions were scored by hand based on correct identification of each letter rule (+1 per letter, -0.5 for spurious extra rules). The second experimental system was a custom ALP reactor simulation controlled via a tab-separated recipe file format, using a gemini-2.5-pro ReACT agent with a gemini-2.5-flash summarization sub-agent. The agent had two tools: perform_experiment (submits a recipe string to the simulator and receives pressure and QCM sensor narratives) and retrieve_experiment (retrieves full experiment data on demand). Four reactor configurations were tested. Configuration I used two fictitious chemicals A and B with favorable reaction kinetics for self-limiting deposition, run in 3 iterations with 3600s of allocated experimental time. Configuration II used the same two chemicals but with slower kinetics and lower vapor pressure for chemical B, tested under three prompting conditions: IIa (same prompt as I, 3600s), IIb (increased time to 7200s), and IIc (7200s plus a reference QCM value for a monolayer). Each condition was run for 3 iterations. Configuration III expanded the chemical space to four chemicals (A, B, C, D) enabling ALD, ALE, passivation, CVD co-dose, and CVD decomposition processes, run for 3 iterations with 7200s and nudging prompts to prevent premature termination. A reference expert recipe was also run to generate a labeled dataset for UMAP visualization; the full reactor state (560-dimensional vectors) was subsampled via k-means and projected into 2D using UMAP trained on the expert run to visualize agent experimental trajectories against expert-labeled process regions. The reactor simulation itself modeled a 1m tube discretized into N sections, solving coupled reactive transport PDEs including advection, diffusion (Bosanquet relation), and surface coverage equations with Arrhenius reaction kinetics, Antoine equation vapor pressures, and Hagen-Poiseuille pressure drop, with pressure and QCM sensors as the only outputs available to the agent.
